sections.h2: Your options for selling in Cortlandt
sections.html:
Cortlandt homeowners generally choose among a broker listing, a handshake sale with a known buyer, and a straight cash purchase. Cash earns its place when repairs are piling up, mortgage or tax payments have slipped, an estate needs closing out, or the calendar leaves no room for delay.

Fixing a house up for market costs money and time before anyone walks through. A cash buyer skips that step, buys the place flaws and all, and lowers the number to match. Compare every offer with what you still owe the lender, any tax balance and your closing costs.

  • Broker listing: best for a house in good shape when you can wait for the right buyer.
  • Private sale: works if you trust the buyer and can handle a contract.
  • Cash sale: built for deferred maintenance, inherited homes, tenant trouble or a tax penalty about to grow.

Cortlandt is a Westchester County town of about 42,413 people, up the Hudson from the city. It includes the villages of Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson and hamlets such as Cortlandt Manor, Montrose, Crugers and Verplanck. Metro-North stops at the Cortlandt and Croton-Harmon stations, and the mean commute is 37.8 minutes, which buyers weigh when they price a house here. Commuters often ask about train access first, so mention the nearest station in your sale description. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $579,500, a useful yardstick when you weigh offers.

The Tax Receiver collects for five school districts: Croton-Harmon, Hendrick Hudson, Lakeland, Putnam Valley and Yorktown. School taxes can differ sharply between houses only a few miles apart, so say which district the property is in whenever you share details with a buyer.

Village lines add another bill. Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson levy their own village taxes, billed separately from the Town and County bill. For a house within village limits, call the village office for that bill and its schedule. The Tax Receiver's office page links to both villages.

Westchester towns act as collection agents, so the Cortlandt Tax Receiver bills Town, County and school taxes. The Town and County bill goes out by April 1 and is due April 30. The school bill goes out by September 1 and can be paid in full by September 30 or in two halves, the first by September 30 and the second by January 31.

  • Town and County penalty: 2% in May, 5% in June and July, 7% in August and September, 10% from October to December and 12% from January to April.
  • School first half: 2% in October, 5% in November, 7% in December and January, 10% in February and March, 12% in April.
  • No Town employee can waive a penalty.
  • Prior-year taxes unpaid by June 30 become a lien on July 1, and a property with taxes unpaid after 21 months can be foreclosed.

The Receiver's office is at 1 Heady Street in Cortlandt Manor, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. and on the last Saturday of April and September from 9 a.m. to noon. More than 15,000 parcels are billed from there. After hours, a courtyard drop box accepts payments, but not cash. Online payment adds a $1.00 fee for e-check or a 1.81% third-party fee for cards. Mailed payments need a United States postmark on or before the due date, since postage meter marks do not count.

Cortlandt runs on its own calendar. May 1 is tax status day, which is also the deadline for exemptions and tax map changes. The tentative roll is published June 1, Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in June, and the final roll appears September 15. The 2027 Grievance Day falls on Tuesday, June 15.

The prior year's final roll sets the current year's taxes. A grievance disputes the assessed value, not the bill itself. Before filing, ask yourself honestly whether the house would really sell for the full market value on the roll. Form RP-524 must be filed with the Assessment Office even if you plan to appear before the Board, and a mailed copy must arrive by 8 p.m. on Grievance Day.

Senior citizen and disability exemptions with limited income renew every year. The Assessor mails renewal forms in February and wants them back with supporting papers by May 1. Selling a house that has one? Let the buyer know the break stays with you as the owner, and a new owner must apply on their own. Enhanced STAR has no application, because the state verifies income yearly.

The Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk files deeds, mortgages and satisfactions and accepts them electronically. Cover pages, Form TP-584 transfer tax returns and RP-5217 reports are created through the clerk's PREP portal. Deeds go back to 1680 in its online search.

The state transfer tax runs $2 per $500 of consideration. Sellers usually cover it, and the return plus payment must reach the state within 15 days of delivering the deed. A sale at $1 million or above adds a 1% tax charged to the buyer. For permits and open violations, start with the Town and, for village addresses, the village hall.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or work undone
sections.html:
Owe something on the house? Phone the Tax Receiver before agreeing to a price and request the exact amount owed with penalties added. Whatever it is gets taken from the sale proceeds, so get the number in writing early. Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson owners should ask their village for the same.

Going cash removes repair lists, open houses and a lender's appraisal. It leaves in place the title work, the deed, the transfer return and any lien payoffs. Pull together your loan statement, newest tax bill, exemption letters and permit notes, and offers can be weighed quickly.

sections.h2: Closing timeline for a cash sale
sections.html:
Step one is the paper trail. Step two is a walk-through followed by an offer. After a contract is signed, the title company searches records and surfaces any lien or tax balance. Those payoffs are subtracted from what you receive when the sale closes.

Once the deed is signed, Form TP-584 carries the transfer tax return, and the cover page and RP-5217 come out of the PREP portal before the County Clerk records the deed. Have your attorney or title company say who files what, so no piece lingers beyond 15 days.

faqs.q: Does a Cortlandt house need repairs before it can be sold for cash?
faqs.a: Not usually. Cash purchasers buy as-is and subtract the repair cost from their price, so your number will sit under a fixed-up listing. Check for open permits or violations beforehand.

faqs.q: When is the next Grievance Day in Cortlandt?
faqs.a: It lands on Tuesday, June 15, 2027, the third Tuesday of June. Exemption applications are separate and due May 1.

faqs.q: Who collects property taxes in Cortlandt?
faqs.a: The Tax Receiver at 1 Heady Street handles Town, County and school bills. Village taxes in Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson come from the villages.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the April 30 Town and County tax date?
faqs.a: The bill picks up 2% in May and 5% in June and July. Nobody at the Town can waive it, so pay quickly.

faqs.q: Where is a Cortlandt deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk, in White Plains. Attach Form TP-584 and create the cover page in the PREP portal.
